rv.q: As a double bill, of sorts, the first is the showcase, not only of its two central performers but the power of performance itself.
It is not a simple double bill but a singular, enthralling work of art that lingers long after the final bow.
Electra/Persona is an intense, strange, compelling hybrid: measured but pacy; part cinema, part theatre; pretentious but emotionally accessible, too.
Savour Electra though – because it's visually arresting and Blanchett and Hoss conjure up literal theatrical sparks of electricity.

cn.t: Critics praise this audacious theatrical event, with Blanchett and Hoss conjuring "literal theatrical electricity" in a thrilling mash-up of Greek tragedy and Bergman that delivers on its bold premise.
